title: Structure Solution of a Quasicrystal Approximant Embedded Within an Aluminum Matrix by SPED and 3DED
content: Electron crystallography has – in recent years – seen considerable growth, and three-dimensional electron diffraction (3DED) techniques have proved viable for solving single crystal structures [1]. As such, extending our area of inquiry into more complex systems seems feasible. By combining 3DED with scanning precession electron diffraction (SPED), are we able to solve the structure of nanosized inclusions in metallic matrices? In the following work, we solve the structure of an α-Al(Mn,Fe)Si particle embedded in an aluminum (Al) sample using three different 3DED data collection protocols. We report and compare the structure models generated by each method, and evaluate the techniques’ respective merits.
